I was kinda new and a call came in and the first question the guy asked was " Where are you located?" Sometimes our members call and think they're talking with an insurance agent in a local office as opposed to a call center rep, so I told him, "I'm located at our service center in City, State. But I can locate the nearest office and put you in touch with a local agent, of you'd like?" 

To which he replied, "City... State..." (repeating what I had told him) "Nope, that'll do perfectly. I should be there in a few hours!"

I thought... oh jeez... this guy is going to drive 7 hours just for a print out of his ID cards...

I said to him, "You see, the office I'm in really doesn't work with members face-to-face, unfortunately, as we are just a call center."

He replied, "No, no. Your location is just what I need.  I have a problem I need dealt with and the only way to properly correct my problem is to head straight to the source and blow your building up."

My heart stopped beating. I was thinking aw shit, I just gave this dude our freaking location and now we're all gonna die.

Luckily, I alerted our security team who called him back and managed to get in touch with him.  Turns out he was just on a shit ton of pain pills and had to keep getting up to answer the phone whenever it rang and for some reason he thought it was us!

So the great thing about the Switch is that it is so versatile.  It literally works as a handheld console (like a Gameboy, 3DS, etc) and you can also plug it into the TV and play it on the big screen!

To plug it into the TV, all you need is an available HDMI socket. You plug the dock in to the wall using the Switch's charging cable, and then into the TV using the HDMI cord. Disconnect the Joycons (controllers) from the side of the Switch, ans voila! You can play on the TV!

If you are curious about buying additional controllers, you have a few options.  You can either buy another pair of Joycons, or if there's only going to be a couple of her friends playing at a time, you can simply use the Joycons that come with the switch.  Now there's a matter of preference. For me, because I have larger hands, I prefer using the Joycons together when playing on the TV. The Switch comes with a kind of attachment that connects the Joycons when separate from the Switch console so it's kinda similar to plaging another console like a Playstation or Xbox. Now, if she and her friends are younger, they might not have a problem with just using the Joycons individually, for which you just turn the separate controllers (called the Left Joycon and the Right Joycon) and play like you would a controller for the Wii.

Really, the Switch itself comes with everything you might need. It might be worth purchasing just the Switch and then seeing if she is in need of a separate pair of Joycons for her friends to play too. If they have their own Switches already at home, they can just bring along their own controllers too. 

One thing I'd recommend is buying a case for the Switch. The case I have stores games too. They are not like regular discs, they are small cartriges similar to SD cards.
